newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says Nigeria owes it $117 mln.
newsitem.headline: Shell says Nigeria owes it $117 mln.

text.p: Nigeria's military government owes Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, $117 million in cash call arrears, a company spokesman said.
"We are also owed cash calls of 16.75 billion naira in local currency as at March 18," the spokesman said at the weekend in Lagos.
Cash calls are payments by the government through state oil company Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) to its six foreign joint venture partners.
Apart from Shell, the Nigerian government is in partnership with Chevron Nigeria, Elf Nigeria, Agip Nigeria, Mobil Nigeria and Texaco.
The Shell spokesman said: "We are all facing difficult times as cash calls arrears have been on steady increase since last year."
The government said when it announced the fiscal budget in January that it approved a budget of $2 billion, same as last year, for cash call payments in 1997.
The multinationals complained their operations were being adversely affected as the government budget represented a 40 percent cut in the $3.32 billion budget they presented collectively.
"We have been discussing with NNPC to see what could be done with settling the arrears owed us as well as revisiting this year's budget," the Shell spokesman said.
The company said on Monday it was losing 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil after shutting six flow stations because of a feud between two villages.
But the output cut would not affect crude exports by Shell, which produces almost half of Nigeria's two million bpd of crude.
